Reverse matches the reference coin. It says "Asu Naba". The Naba definitely refers to "Nawab". "Asu" could be Yusuf Khan aka Marudhnayam according to [this | https://www.facebook.com/manikandan.prabhu.56/posts/pfbid0ehREyBrVeEEsb9ctPbkEkgC3v7t5Tb2PPbyg24CE2fvqogGQFRrUCcKkcJCLY6ql].  There is also a full discussion on coins with AsuNaba in the [monogram on Arcot coins | https://govtmuseumchennai.org/uploads/topics/16527873255719.pdf]. Weight does not match though

No match in Zeno or Numista. Obverse is peacock. Peacock was commonly used by Mahfuz Khan, who was brother of Wallajah. He later rebelled. The reverse clearly shows Wallajah. Page 89 of this [doc | https://govtmuseumchennai.org/uploads/topics/16527873255719.pdf] has this coin clearly called out
